JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 05-03-2024 at about 01-30 pm., the petitioner was proceeding in his Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KD-4842 on Magadi main road and when he reached near Bangalore Magadi main road, in front of Parisharama granait, forest gate,
Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore city, at that time the driver of Tata ACE MEGA XL bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-4446 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle from behind, result of which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Kenganar Hospital, Bangalore, wherein took treatment as an inpatient for a period of 3 days with an advise to continue follow up treatment.
So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 32 years.

He was working as Civil Engineering Contractor work at NEXT DESIGN AND BUILD, Nagasandra,
Bangalore and earning monthly Rs.50,000/-. Due to the accidental injuries
, he has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. On service of notice, the Respondent no.1 did not appear before the tribunal, remained absent and hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. The Respondent no.2 /insurer of Tata ACE MEGA XL bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-4446 has filed written statement and contended that there is delay in lodging the complaint and that Tata Ace vehicle was falsely implicated by the petitioner in collusion with the owner and the police official to get compensation from the respondent no.2, that petition is liable to be dismissed for non joinder of necessary parties as owner and insurer of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KD-4842, Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-JM-7765 are necessary parties, that the petition filed after the limitation period and that the driver of Tata Ace vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence and there was no permit and FC to the vehicle of the respondent no.1 to ply the vehicle on the road.
It is further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner, who was not holding driving license and he was not wearing the helmet.

sentences.text:
On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained injuries on account of road traffic accident on 05-03-2024 at about 01-30 p.m., on Bangalore Magadi main road,
Infornt of Parisharama granait, forest gate, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of TATA ACE MEGA XL bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB-4446?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3
. What order or award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and one witness is examined as P.W.2 and they got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P14 and closed evidence from his side.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident that took place on 05-03-2024 at about 01-30 pm., when the petitioner was proceeding in his Motorcycle bearing No.KA-04-KD-4842 on Magadi main road and when he reached near Bangalore - Magadi main road, in front of Parisharama granait, forest gate, Dasanapura Hobli, Bangalore city, at that time the driver of Tata ACE MEGA XL bearing Reg.No.KA-04-AB- 4446 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle from behind, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 7 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint, Spot mahazar, sketch, wound certificate, notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act and reply given there on, IMV report, charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sunil N. case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0206/2024 by Madanayakanahalli Police Station for the offence Sunil N vs Naveen Kumar L on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76327324/
3 punishable under section 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC.

sentences.text:
After completion of investigation, the investigating officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC.
13.

So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, as per the case of the petitioner, at the time of accident he was proceeding in his motorcycle from Bangalore- Magadi main road and when he reached in front of Parisharama granait, forest gate, Dasanapur Hobli, the offending vehicle which came from behind hit to his vehicle.
The Learned counsel for respondent no.2 while cross examining the PW.1 has posed suggestion that the petitioner all of a sudden took his vehicle towards right side and hit to the offending vehicle.
The PW.1 denied the said suggestion.
The petitioner has produced the spot mahazar and rough sketch marked as Ex.P2 and 3.
If the documents are perused, the width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 28 feet.
The accident in question has occurred at a distance of nearly 8 feet from the left edge of tar road towards right side.

Though the Learned counsel for respondent no.2 by referring the IMV report wherein there is mention about the damage caused to the motorcycle of the petitioner on the front portion, has submitted that the accident in question has occurred not in the manner stated by the petitioner and that if the offending vehicle hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner on its rear side then the rear portion of the motorcycle would have been damaged instead on front portion.
14. If the complaint, FIR and charge sheet is perused, in all three vehicles were involved in the accident.

According to the petitioner, after the offending vehicle was hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner on its rear side it proceeded ahead and hit to the Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing Reg.no.KA-04-JM -7765 on its rear side.
If IMV report at Ex.P6 is perused, the front portion of the offending vehicle was damaged.
Further the rear portion of the Bajaj Pulsar motorcycle bearing no.KA-04-JM-7765 was damaged.
It is true that so far as vehicle of the petitioner is concerned, the front wheel mudguard was damaged.

If really the offending vehicle has not hit to the motorcycle of the petitioner on its rear side so also the pulsar motorcycle bearing No.KA- 04-JM-7765 on its rear side there was no possibility of causing damage on the front portion of the offending vehicle.

Hence,
merely because no damage was caused on the rear portion of the motorcycle of the petitioner it cannot be said that the offending vehicle has not hit to the petitioner vehicle on its rear side.

Though the respondent no.2 has disputed the manner of accident but nowhere either in the written statement or in the evidence has stated the manner in which according to them the accident in question has occurred.
Admittedly the respondent no.1 who is the owner of the offending vehicle has remained ex-parte.
The respondent no.2 has not opted to lead the evidence of respondent no.2 or the driver of the offending vehicle.
Hence, by relying upon the bald statement of the respondent no.2 it cannot be said that accident in question has not occurred in the manner stated by the petitioner.
When petitioner was proceeding ahead of the offending vehicle, the driver of the offending vehicle ought to have maintained minimum distance between the two vehicle.
It is nowhere the case of the respondent no.2 that the petitioner suddenly applied break or suddenly stopped the vehicle result of which this mishap has occurred.

When there is no rebuttal evidence on this point, by relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the police documents it can be said that rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P4 and P8.
On going through the medical documents it reveal that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Kenganar Hospital, Bangalore from 05-03-2024 to 07-03-2024 for a period of 3 days.
As per the wound certificate, petitioner has sustained one injury which is grievous in nature.
16. Dr. Ramesh B. - Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore is examined as Pw-2 and through him OPD and x-ray film are got marked as Ex.P13 and Ex.P14.
The PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner on 20-07-2025 clinically, radiological for assessment of disability.

PW.2 further deposed that petitioner has suffered permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 16%
and to the whole body at 8% and that the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants.
17. If the cross examination of PW.2 is perused, he is not a treated doctor and the fracture injury of the petitioner is united and there is no shorting of limb.
If the medical documents are perused, the petitioner has sustained only one injury and has taken treatment only for three days and his fracture is united.

Further as per the judgment reported in 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk, the normal rule would be disability in the lower limb would be 1/3rd of the particular limb.

entities.text: 2014 (4) Kar.L.J 157 Vijaya Kumar Alias Babu Rao Vs The Secretary, Agricultural Produce Marketing Committee Balki, Taluk
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, this court inclines to assess the disability of the petitioner at 5% instead of 8% on whole body.
With the disability of 5%, the petitioner can do his personal and professional work and the said amount of disability would not come in the way of his future earnings.
At the most the said percentage of disability may have caused some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.

Hence,
petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head future loss of income but he is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.
18.
Hence, considering the nature of injuries sustained, period of treatment taken this court is of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for compensation under different heads.
19. Towards pain and sufferings, petitioner shown to have sustained one grievous injury.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injury sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
20. So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, he has produced 10 medical bills for Rs.1,08,027/- as per Ex.P10.
As such petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,08,027/- under the head medical expenses.
21. It is stated that petitioner was working as Civil Engineering Contractor work at NEST DESIGN AND BUILD, Nagasandra, Bangalore.
But, he has not produced any document to prove his income and avocation.
Hence this court considering the age of the petitioner, the year of accident and place of residence considers the income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

sentences.text: The petitioner has sustained one grievous injury and taken treatment for 3 days as an inpatient in Kenganar Hospital.
Hence, it is reasonable to hold that period of three months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of the petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation this Tribunal takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m for three months.

Hence petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.49,500/- towards loss of income during the laid down period.
23.
From the evidence of Pw.1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment at Kenganar Hospital.
For 03 days of hospitalization requires an attendant, was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and need further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.

Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs,20,000/-
taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
24. So far as future medical expenses is concerned, even though PW.2 has deposed that petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implant.
But he has not given any estimation
Hence, this court awards compensation under the head future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- and entitled for sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head loss of amenities and discomfort.

Thereby petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Under the Heads Amount No. (in Rupees )
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Medical expenses Rs. 1,08,027/-
 3. Towards loss of income during Rs. 49,500/-
 laid up period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 20,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  5. Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000/-
 6. Loss of amenities and discomfort.

Rs. 1,00,000/-
 Total Rs. Rs.3,77,527/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.3,77,527/- (Rupees Three Lakh Seventy Seven Thousand Five Hundred Twenty Seven only).
25. As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent No.2 this Tribunal directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
26. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,77,527/- + cost of Rs.3,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.IV & V.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.3,80,527/- (Rupees Three Lakh Eighty Thousand Five Hundred Twenty Seven only).

After deducting cost of Rs.3000/- and future medical expenses to the tune of Rs.30,000/- balance sum of Rs.3,47,527/- shall carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the said amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
